Who Took the Cake? Rules

A detective puzzle with a friendly case: one of the animals took the cake, and the clues tell you which one.

The rules

The floor plan
The board is a floor plan of N x N cells. Thick lines split it into rooms, and each room's name stands at the top of one of its cells. Some cells hold furniture: a table, chair, rug, plant or cupboard. A window hangs on the outer wall of one row.
What you place
You place N things: N-1 animals (dog, cat, rabbit, mouse and hedgehog, depending on the level) and the cake. Every row and every column holds exactly one of them.
Furniture
The cake always stands on a table. Animals never stand on a table, a cupboard or a plant - these fill their whole cell in the picture. A chair or rug is drawn small in a corner: an animal may stand there.
The clues
Every animal has at least one clue below the board, for example “The dog is in the garden”, “The cat sits on a chair” or “The mouse is next to a plant” (directly beside it, not diagonally). “Next to” only counts within the same room: furniture on the other side of a wall is not next to the animal. Together the clues leave only one way to place everything, and you never need to guess.
Who took the cake?
Exactly one animal is in the same room as the cake. That animal took it.
Playing
Choose a button below the board - an animal, the cake, or X for “nothing here” - then tap a cell. Tapping the same cell again with the same choice takes it off. Tap a clue to tick it off. The Hint button points out a mistake first; otherwise it places the animal that can be worked out next. The cake you place yourself: once all animals stand, the hint only tells you that one row and one column are left.
Levels
Easy: 4x4 with 3 animals and simple steps. Medium: 5x5 with 4 animals. Hard: 6x6 with 5 animals and longer chains of reasoning.

A solved example

The picture shows a solved 4x4 puzzle. Every row and every column holds one thing, the cake stands on a table, and the only animal in the cake's room - the cat, in the kitchen - took the cake.

Finishing a puzzle

Solved
The puzzle is solved as soon as the cake stands in its right place. All the animals are then shown in their places, and the message names the animal that took the cake.
